Architecture

Zone/server/backend topology

One zone simulation per early dedicated process; one authenticated backend and one relational database.

On this page
Deployment topologyService stack decisionAuthentication provider boundaryCapacity and failure domains

Deployment topology

Client A -> Zone_A Rillmere, Client B -> Zone_A Rillmere. Zone_A and Zone_B Thornweald -> authenticated GameService -> PostgreSQL. The frontend talks to identity/roster/admission endpoints; game clients never connect to SQL. After a gate handoff Client A connects to Zone_B while Client B remains on Zone_A.

A later dungeon is another compatible instance process/reservation, not a local loading shortcut. A future allocator may host multiple processes on a machine, but process count, world size, player count and regions are separate dimensions.

Service stack decision

Compare ASP.NET Core/.NET10 with a single Node.js/TypeScript service. Both can implement a small authenticated API and PostgreSQL transactions. Select .NET10 here for typed request models, maintained long-term support and straightforward single-service deployment; this is a project preference, not an engine requirement. The developer must verify current provider package/ORM versions before installation.

Use parameterized PostgreSQL access and one migration path. Either explicit SQL migrations plus typed handlers or a compatible EF Core provider is viable; this edition favors explicit migration SQL specifications and a thin typed data-access layer for transparent row locks. Avoid a second ORM or event bus until there is a demonstrated need.

Authentication provider boundary

An authenticator verifies a provider proof and maps issuer+subject to AccountId. EOS may be evaluated behind that interface after installed/version/provider compatibility testing. Provider login is not a wallet, inventory database or zone allocator. Development fixture auth must be loopback/private-only and impossible to select in production startup.

Capacity and failure domains

Allocator reserves compatible capacity before issuing a transfer ticket. Count active sessions plus in-flight reservations. Health signals prevent new admissions to a bad process but do not themselves transfer character write authority; the session epoch/lease does that. If the backend is unavailable, never create local save truth to keep an economic action appearing successful.

Evidence and external references

External links need internet; the manual itself remains offline. Public documentation does not prove installed compatibility.

  • Setting up dedicated servers — Public 5.8 tutorial checked; its dedicated-server build route requires a C++ project and source engine build. No target built here.
  • Online Services — Public overview checked; provider capabilities and beta shipping limitations require provider/version-specific verification.
  • .NET support lifecycle — Official table checked: .NET 10 support runs to 2028-11-14/15 depending on display timezone. Patch version must be pinned locally.
  • PostgreSQL transaction isolation — Official current documentation resolved to PostgreSQL 18; transaction isolation and whole-transaction retry requirements checked.
